---
title: "check-term-links.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, blocking check that every technical term is linked to its
definition the first time it appears in each div, or in each paragraph outside
a div.
This is the lab's linking rule
([ai-config#4553](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/ai-config/pull/4553),
[psw#223](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/223),
[psw#227](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psw/pull/227));
the check is
[gha#1078](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1078).

## Which words are terms

The check learns them from the files it scans, so it needs no list:

- **Definition divs.**
  Each `::: {#def-...}` div contributes its title (any heading inside it)
  and its bold terms.
  A parenthetical gloss, and an alias after a comma, `or`, `also called`
  or `known as`, is split into its own term.
- **Links to definitions.**
  Each link whose target ends in `#def-...` contributes its link text.
  This is how a term defined on another site becomes known:
  `[risk](https://example.com/ch.html#def-risk)` anywhere in the corpus makes
  "risk" a term.
- **A terms file.**
  `terms-file` adds terms by hand, one per line.

A term is one to five words of letters, at least three characters, and not
a label such as "note" or "example".
`allow-file` removes terms that are ordinary English in the corpus.

## What it flags

- **`unlinked-first-use`.**
  The first occurrence of a known term in a passage is plain text.
  A passage is one div (between its fences), or one paragraph outside divs.
  An occurrence inside a link, or followed by `(@def-...)`, is linked.
  A term's own definition div is skipped,
  and so is any other div in the file that holds that definition
  (such as a source callout).
  A paragraph outside divs is still checked.
  The plural of a term counts as the term, and the longest term wins, so
  "test set" is not also a use of "set".
- **`partial-link`.**
  A link covers only part of a longer defined phrase,
  such as "logistic [regression](...)" when "logistic regression" is defined.
  Link the whole phrase to its own definition.
- **`no-definition`.**
  A bold term in a passage that is not a definition div, and that matches no
  known term: it is introduced as technical and defined nowhere.
  Give it a `#def-` div and link to it.
  Bold function words ("not", "once") are ignored.

It skips code fences and spans, math, HTML comments, YAML front matter,
include shortcodes, headings, images, and the target of a link.
`<!-- check-term-links: allow -->` exempts a line, and
`<!-- check-term-links: ignore-file -->` a file.

## Scope

Terms are always learned from every tracked file the globs match.
Findings are reported only on lines the pull request adds, so adopting the
check does not reflag what the corpus already carries.
With no `base-ref`, the check skips with a warning instead of widening to the
whole tree; `whole-tree: true` asks for that scan on purpose, to measure a
corpus.

## Usage

```yaml
jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-term-links.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   terms-file: .github/terms.txt
    #   allow-file: .github/terms-allow.txt
    #   fail: true
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Space-separated git pathspecs of files to learn from and check |
| `paths-ignore` | `''` | Comma/newline-separated globs to skip (`*`, `?`, `**`) |
| `terms-file` | `''` | File of extra terms, one per line |
| `allow-file` | `''` | File of terms to leave alone, one per line |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Report every finding, not only those on added lines |
| `fail` | `true` | Fail the job on a finding (`false`: warning annotations only) |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version to set up |
| `runs-on` | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

The reusable workflow needs only `contents: read`.
